newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi moving about, holding meetings.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi moving about, holding meetings.

text.p: Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi has left her residence recently and has been holding meetings with senior members of her National League for Democracy (NLD) party, NLD sources said on Sunday.

The sources said Suu Kyi, who last week was urged to stay in her compound to avoid meeting with student protesters, had attended a birthday party on Saturday and also met with various party officials at her residence.
Last week a senior NLD official said Suu Kyi, who was released from six years of house arrest in July 1995, was being held a virtual prisoner in her house.

A government official denied the accusation, but told Reuters on Friday security officials from the government and the NLD had urged the Nobel Peace laureate not to leave her house during student protests held last week.

Up to 1,000 university students held rare sit-in protests at an intersection about two km (1.2 miles) from Suu Kyi's residence. They were protesting against the government's handling of a scuffle between students and restuarant owners.
The government accused the NLD of colluding with the students and trying to politicise the altercation to foment unrest.

The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) questioned Suu Kyi's close aide, Kyi Maung, on Wednesday morning for his role in the protests. Kyi Maung, who has not yet been released, was seen talking to two of the student leaders before the demonstrations.
The NLD source said over the past week Suu Kyi had held meetings at her home, and the NLD officials who attended the meetings were brought there by government transport.

All roads leading to Suu Kyi's street have been blocked, and no vehicles or pedestrians are allowed to enter. But the government arranged last week to escort the NLD members Suu Kyi wanted to meet past the blockades to her house.
The barricades, which have been up for most of the past month in an effort to stop major meetings of democracy activists, were still in place on Sunday.
Suu Kyi has been unable to give her regular weekend speeches to supporters since late September when the barricades were first erected.

The SLORC has said the weekend gatherings are illegal, and could bring about unrest. Suu Kyi vowed to continue the speeches -- her only overt way to spread the NLD message to supporters -- as soon as the roadblocks were lifted.
The NLD won a landslide victory in a 1990 election, but the SLORC never recognised the results.
